transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-04-12
Time: 15:00 UTC (08:00 PT)
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Myers (Redwood AE), Evelyn Chen (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Alvarez (Northpoint - Head of ML), Tom Rowe (Northpoint - Platform Eng), Sonia Gupta (Northpoint - CTO), Jordan Li (Northpoint - Security)

Summary:
Quick clinic-style demo focused on JSON-mode structured output, safe tool invocation patterns, and how Redwood Console + Optimize can run a short pilot to measure latency/cost tradeoffs. Customer wants to understand guardrails for action calls, private deployment options (VPC/on-prem), and end-to-end pilot steps.

Topics covered:
- JSON mode (typed responses, action schemas)
- Runtime sandboxing/safe tool calling and fallback behavior
- Console runbook for rollouts, canaries and A/Bs
- Redwood Optimize suggestions (batching, quantization, cache) to reduce token cost
- Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private tradeoffs (latency, cost, data residency)
- Security: SOC2, KMS, audit logs, SSO/SAML, RBAC
- Pilot mechanics and acceptance criteria (latency, cost per token, accuracy)

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan Myers: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh this is Jordan from Redwood AE. I'll hand it off to Evelyn to kick off the demo.
[00:12] Evelyn Chen: hey all, Evelyn here. Quick agenda — show JSON-mode contract enforcement, demonstrate a tool invoke sandbox, then walk through the Console Optimize suggestions and how you'd run a pilot. we'll sprinkle in Q&A as we go. sound good?
[00:24] Maya Alvarez: yes sounds good. main thing for us is we want to avoid silent failures — when the model calls our downstream actions we need strong typing and safe fallbacks. also, our infra team is nervous about running anything public.
[00:36] Samir Patel: totally get it. we'll show both hosted path plus private options. the runtime has a sandbox that can simulate tool responses and then you can flip to real invocation once a canary passes.
[00:48] Evelyn Chen: ok jumping into a quick Console view — apologies if the screencast is a bit choppy. this is the 'JSON mode' playground: you register a schema for the response, and the runtime validates each generated output against the schema and will auto-retry with a stricter prompt if it fails.
[01:12] Tom Rowe: wait, auto-retry? does that mean we get mutated outputs until it matches and costs go up?
[01:18] Evelyn Chen: good question — you can set a retry budget. by default it's conservative: 1 retry with a fallback route. Optimize will flag high-retry prompts and suggest prompt edits or a schema relaxation. so you have observability before costs blow up.
[01:30] Jordan Li: on the security side, if the runtime retries and calls our webhook, does it leak anything in headers or tokens? how are credentials handled?
[01:38] Samir Patel: credentials never flow through the public runtime in plaintext. for hosted flows we do a tokenized callback, and customers can use per-route credentials with short-lived tokens. for Private (VPC) deployments, you provide the service endpoint and KMS or HSM keys remain on your side.
[01:50] Sonia Gupta: can you show the tool invocation flow — like a step where the model asks to call 'create_shipment' and we want to validate the payload?
[01:58] Evelyn Chen: yep. here's an example schema for create_shipment (I've redacted some fields). notice required fields, enums for service type, and a nested address contract. when the model returns an action, the console shows a validation pass/fail. if it fails, you can configure 3 things: block, sanitize+pass, or sandbox.
[02:22] Maya Alvarez: sandbox how? emulate the downstream?
[02:25] Evelyn Chen: exactly — sandbox mode will route to a replay service that returns canned responses. you can iterate on prompts and schema without hitting production. once happy, you switch to live invocation and the runtime will do a canary: first N requests to a staging cluster, metrics compared to baseline, then ramp.
[02:40] Jordan Myers: and we provide hooks for tracing — each invocation has a trace id in the Console UI so you can link model token breakdown, validation result, and the actual HTTP call.
[02:50] Tom Rowe: latency... what's the expected added latency when invoking a tool synchronously through the runtime? we need sub-250ms for some front-line uses.
[02:58] Samir Patel: depends on deployment. hosted API median can be 120–200ms for small models under typical load; for strict SLOs we'd recommend Dedicated capacity or Private in-region deployment. Dedicated gives you reserved GPUs and predictable scheduling; you can get tail latency down by adjusting batching thresholds and KV cache warm-up.
[03:18] Maya Alvarez: ok but cost tradeoffs — Dedicated can be big commit. we want a pilot that demonstrates both cost & latency with our traffic profile.
[03:25] Evelyn Chen: yep — Optimize will generate cost profiles if you upload a sample traffic CSV. it will suggest batching, tokenization tweaks, and quantization levels. we'll include that in the pilot SOW.
[03:36] [04:00] Evelyn Chen: switching gears — show a live run where the model produces a typed action: {"action":"create_shipment","args":{...}}. Console shows validation green, then you can click 'simulate' or 'invoke'. hitting simulate returns a canned 200.
[04:20] Maya Alvarez: i see a small correction: zipcode field got parsed as string vs int — that's a common noise in our corpus. can you coerce?
[04:27] Evelyn Chen: yes we support coercion rules in the schema. you can also add pre-processors or an inline transform that normalizes fields before validation.
[04:36] Sonia Gupta: ...what about hallucinations where the model invents a carrier code that doesn't exist?
[04:40] Samir Patel: that's where the 'external validator' step helps — you can configure a post-validate hook to check against your master data and reject or enrich. and the runtime will automatically fallback to a safe path if post-validate fails.
[04:55] Tom Rowe: is that synchronous? will the user wait?
[04:58] Evelyn Chen: you can choose sync or async semantics: if low latency is critical, we recommend enqueueing and returning an optimistic response while the actual invocation runs async. Console supports both patterns and the audit/logs show eventual state.
[05:10] Maya Alvarez: about logs — we need tamper-evident audit logs for compliance. how is that surfaced?
[05:15] Samir Patel: all events are append-only and can be exported to your SIEM. for Private deployments you keep logs on-prem and integrate with your ELK/Splunk. for hosted, we provide signed log bundles and support syslog export.
[05:29] Jordan Li: KMS integration — can we use our AWS KMS + a customer-managed key?
[05:33] Evelyn Chen: yes for Private/ VPC you bring your KMS. for Hosted we support envelope encryption with customer-managed keys via cross-account roles — keys never leave AWS KMS.
[05:43] [07:00] Evelyn Chen: demo: now i flip to the 'failure' scenario. model returns a malformed JSON payload. runtime triggers an auto-rewrite prompt and we get a second generation that corrects the schema. Console flags the token delta from the rewrite.
[07:24] Tom Rowe: nice. will Optimize flag prompts that frequently require rewrites?
[07:28] Jordan Myers: yes, Optimize shows a delta heatmap of prompts with high rewrite rates. it can also suggest moving validation earlier in the pipeline or adding more constrained templates.
[07:40] Maya Alvarez: about pilot acceptance criteria — our bar is 95th percentile latency <= 300ms for sync create_shipment calls, and <1% schema failures after retry. can you measure that?
[07:52] Evelyn Chen: absolutely. we'll instrument the pilot with SLO dashboards in Console and include raw traces so you can audit the results.
[08:02] Sonia Gupta: security review — we'll need SOC2, penetration test results, and a list of third party subprocessors.
[08:08] Jordan Myers: we'll attach the SOC2 and infra whitepaper to the follow-up email. also, Samir can run a security deep-dive with your security team — typical agenda is network diagram, key management, RBAC policies.
[08:20] Jordan Li: do you support IdP SAML provisioning and role-mapping?
[08:24] Samir Patel: yes, SSO via SAML and OIDC, SCIM provisioning, and role-based access controls. we also support fine-grained per-route permissions for who can flip a route to live.
[08:34] Maya Alvarez: ok can we talk about model variants — we run a 13B for cheap vs 70B for quality. can Redwood route by policy?
[08:42] Evelyn Chen: yes routing policies: latency-first, cost-first, region-preference, or custom. you can define a route that tries a smaller model and falls back to a larger one on error or low confidence. the runtime can also do A/B rollout percentages.
[08:54] Tom Rowe: does the confidence signal come from the model or from your scoring layer?
[08:58] Samir Patel: both — we expose model logprobs and a post-hoc scorer in Optimize that can learn from your labeled prompt set. you can tie thresholds to routing decisions.
[09:08] [10:00] Maya Alvarez: what about multi-tenant concerns? we need strict isolation between our business units if we go hosted.
[09:14] Jordan Myers: for multi-tenant in hosted we provide per-tenant isolation logical boundaries, audit tokens, and strict per-customer encryption. but for absolute isolation, customers go Dedicated or Private.
[09:26] Sonia Gupta: let's talk SOW budget — what does a 4-week pilot typically cost and what's included?
[09:31] Jordan Myers: typical pilot includes reserved run time for a week of testing, access to the Console, Optimize analysis, and one SE support block for integration and benchmarking. the SOW will have two options: hosted (low commitment, usage-based) and Dedicated (short-term reserved capacity for predictable latency).
[09:46] Tom Rowe: can we bring our on-prem message bus for callbacks?
[09:49] Evelyn Chen: yes, Private deployment can sit behind your firewall and integrate with internal messaging. we also support secure webhook proxies for hosted if you can't open inbound endpoints.
[09:58] Maya Alvarez: i want to see an end-to-end failure, like the model returns a plausible but incorrect carrier and the post-validate rejects it — what happens to the UX?
[10:06] Evelyn Chen: two options — you can set it to surface a human review workflow (Console shows a queue) or auto-fallback to a safe default route that requests minimal user confirmation. the audit trail keeps original output and rejection reason.
[10:22] Jordan Li: any red-team or fuzz testing you run against the schema enforcement?
[10:26] Samir Patel: yes our onboarding includes a schema-fuzz suite that runs thousands of malformed generations and tracks pass/fail rates; results are in the onboarding report.
[10:34] [12:00] Evelyn Chen: quick note on caching: prefix/KV cache helps with repeated context — Optimize will recommend TTLs. for create_shipment we often cache static carrier metadata which reduces token churn.
[12:18] Maya Alvarez: great. token costs — can we get a projection for our 3 traffic profiles?
[12:23] Jordan Myers: please upload the CSV and we'll run Optimize. we'll include quantization suggestions — sometimes a 4-bit quantized variant saves 30–40% with minimal quality loss on these task flows.
[12:37] Sonia Gupta: any compliance concerns with quantized models?
[12:40] Samir Patel: quantization is at runtime; weights remain within the deployment boundary. with Private you control the hardware and can demand offline attestations.
[12:50] [16:00] Maya Alvarez: ok next steps — timeline wise, we want a pilot start in two weeks. can you confirm feasibility?
[16:08] Jordan Myers: yes target start Apr 26 is feasible if we get artifacts this week (prompts, traffic CSV, security questionnaire).
[16:18] Tom Rowe: i'll upload a redacted traffic file and sample prompts by eod Friday.
[16:22] Jordan Li: i'll consolidate security questions and shoot them over to Jordan.
[16:26] Evelyn Chen: i'll stand up the bench and run an initial g5.48x test with your sample prompts — expect a first-pass latency/cost snapshot in 3 business days.
[16:38] Jordan Myers: i'll send the SOW and a hosted vs dedicated pricing matrix after the call.
[16:44] Maya Alvarez: perfect. also would love a short 'security deep-dive' session for our SecOps next week.
[16:49] Samir Patel: noted — we'll set that up.
[16:52] [20:00] Jordan Myers: any other questions?
[20:05] Sonia Gupta: not right now — this was helpful.
[20:08] Tom Rowe: no more from me.
[20:10] Maya Alvarez: thanks everyone.
[20:12] Jordan Myers: thanks — we'll follow up with notes, SOW and links.
